analogs.covers: How it lives and hunts: the lazy, patient bear of the sea. It rests most of the day, tours the coast after the seals, waits motionless at the breathing hole, stalks submerged and bursts out of the water onto the floe. It prefers seal pups and calves, survives long fasts, and the mother leads her cubs from the den to the sea alone

How it holds ground and keeps cool: the bull guards a small stretch of water with tusk displays and loud bellows before it fights. Its skin flushes pink to dump heat and pales in cold water, it hauls out by the hundreds to bask peacefully, and it lives on shellfish

headline: A polar bear of the sea that guards its home water like a walrus bull: lazy and patient, it tours the Leedsichthys route, then slips under water without a sound and bursts out at the edge.

setting.label: One home sea area, best the cold north (Kelp Vale, Coastal Bluffs), plus tours along the Leedsichthys loop
setting.note: Claims exactly one bright-green sea area on the profile map as its home: best Kelp Vale or the Coastal Bluffs in the north, otherwise Stonebed Shoal or Palm Islands. The Abyssal Depths have no shore to bask or nest on. From home it tours the Leedsichthys migration loop (Kelp Vale, Coastal Bluffs, Palm Islands, Castaway Isle, Stonebed Shoal, back past the Volcano Islands) peacefully and drinks on the way at Rocky Lake, Dark Pond or the lake at Lakeside Meadow, never defending them. Neutral gathering and courtship at Triad Falls, Wollemi Forest and Grand Falls.

playsLike: You are the polar bear among the Spinosaurus. You have one home sea area, ideally Kelp Vale or the Coastal Bluffs in the north. There you nest, defend your water like a walrus bull (sail up, three aggressive calls, then the lunge) and hunt anything up to Apex. Most of your life, though, is lazy: you lie on the beach or a rock with your sail turned to the sun and slip into the water to cool off and keep your skin from cracking. When you get hungry you tour the Leedsichthys migration loop like a bear following the seals, peaceful and without any territorial behaviour, hunting only fish, critters, Leedsichthys and Tylosaurus, their young above all. You wait at the route like a bear at the breathing hole, sink without a sound, glide in under water and burst out. Then you swim home.

why.text: Some Spinosaurus end up "preferring a lazy lifestyle touring saltwater areas, while most possessively claim territory in freshwater lakes and rivers." Polar bears spend most of the day resting and wander the coast after the seals. Their name, Ursus maritimus, means bear of the sea.
"They may hunt Leedsichthys, Tylosaurus, and fish and eat critters anywhere." That is the polar bear's tour: the Leedsichthys loop runs past five sea areas like the seals along the ice edge.

"When hunting, Spinosaurus become alarmingly passive and silent in water." "Rather than aggressing, they silently slip towards their prey." A polar bear swims submerged up to the seal on the floe and bursts out of the water, just as the Spinosaurus lunges from the water.

Against Tylosaurus Spinosaurus "prefer to hunt their offspring due to their more manageable size" and they "enjoy hunting Leedsichthys offspring". Polar bears dig ringed seal pups out of their lairs and take walrus calves, while an adult walrus can kill a bear. An adult Tylosaurus outswims you (900 to 750).
Torpor lets Spinosaurus "survive extended periods without eating or drinking." Pregnant polar bears spend months in the den without food, and Hudson Bay bears fast through the whole summer.

"The blood vessels on the sail help control their body temperature, either absorbing or releasing heat as needed." A walrus does the same with its skin: it flushes pink to dump heat and pales in cold water. Polar bears overheat fast on land and cool off in the water, much as the Spinosaurus needs "frequent dips to keep themselves hydrated."

"To begin this defense, Spinosaurus FIRST display their sail and issue x3 aggressive calls". After 10 seconds it lunges. A walrus bull guards its stretch of water the same way: tusks raised, loud bellows, and only then the fight.

The mother "lures them into the water with gentle calls", hides them with her body and leads them off, while "Their father remains aloof in the early stages". A polar bear mother leads her cubs from the den to the sea alone, and the cubs swim close behind her or ride on her back.

"Young Spinosaurus frequently collect sea shells" to chew on, and at Triad Falls Spinosaurus "gather in large numbers to bask, court and lazily relax." Walruses live on shellfish and haul out by the hundreds. Male polar bears at Churchill gather peacefully and only play-spar.
"Spinosaurus can be fickle over their water source, and move on to new territories when resources are low." Polar bears move with the ice. You still hold only one home area at a time.
Apex tier, 6,000 combat weight, 1,100 HP. Water cruise 500 and sprint 750 for 167 s: level with Leedsichthys (750), slower than adult Tylosaurus (900 for 222 s).

notLike: Polar bears are not territorial; they share huge home ranges. You hold one home sea area and defend it, which is the walrus part.
Polar bears don't drink and get their water from fat. You need fresh water and swim to it outside your home, peacefully and without ever defending it.
Polar bear males are no fathers and even kill cubs. A Spinosaurus seeks one partner for life, and the father guards his brood from a distance.
Outside your home area you are no polar bear on the hunt for everything: you may only take fish, critters, Leedsichthys and Tylosaurus there.
twist: The Tyrannosaurus is a polar bear too, the one on land that waits in cover. You are the polar bear of the sea that comes out of the water. Your freshwater cousin is a grizzly on its river; you are still one species and court together at Triad Falls.
